title: [WT-05] Wrappers: launch every CLI inside the task worktree with per-worktree configs
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §5.1 and §5.2 (configs, agents copy, grok trust; the links are WT-06).

Objective: in worktree mode the agent CLI edits W, never the control checkout, while still reaching the daemon through the control checkout.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- cwd = W for claude, codex (exec -C W), gemini and grok (--cwd W). In ps1 that means Push-Location W for EVERY CLI, including the claude launch that today runs in the launcher's cwd.
- MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays the control checkout. Export MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET from the claim's workspace. The proxy path stays the one resolved from the wrapper's own location.
- Run the existing per-CLI config writers with W as the config root: W/.mcp.json (sh) or the ps1 temp --mcp-config (an interactive sh seat passes --mcp-config W/.mcp.json); W/.codex/config.toml; W/.gemini/settings.json; W/.grok/config.toml plus the grok trust grant for W.
- Copy <control>/.moe/agents/*.md into W/.claude/agents/.
- A config write failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, calls report_blocked and launches no CLI.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Depends on WT-04 (task-c20464ff64ca49fca4371dd9b5194364).

NOT in scope: Serena root, the skills and memories links, the deps notice (WT-06); landing (WT-07 onward); shared-mode launches, which must stay byte-identical; docs (WT-18).

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses, fake CLI that records its cwd and env): in worktree mode the CLI's cwd is W, MOE_PROJECT_PATH is the control checkout, and MOE_WORKTREE_PATH / MOE_TASK_BRANCH / MOE_LAND_TARGET match the claim's workspace.

postflight case: the per-CLI config lands in W (W/.mcp.json or the ps1 temp config, W/.codex/config.toml, W/.gemini/settings.json, W/.grok/config.toml) and the control checkout's copies are not rewritten.
postflight case: W/.claude/agents/*.md equals <control>/.moe/agents/*.md; a forced config-write failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED and launches no CLI.
postflight: every existing shared-mode launch case passes unchanged.
Both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes (grep -oE diff over moe-agent.sh vs moe-agent.ps1 is empty).
The verification command exits 0; postflight.ps1 passes via node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell.

It is DONE before this row can be claimed, because it gates WT-04, which gates this row. The file sits under newFiles only because it did not exist when this plan was written: edit it, never recreate it. Add only. Existing cases, helpers, the cli mode's wt-cli.log line and launch()'s default behaviour stay as they are; QA rejects a weakened held-out test. WT-04 already runs the whole suite from postflight.sh and postflight.ps1, so the new cases run in both harnesses with no harness edit. Landing check, before any edit: run moe.get_commit_scope { taskId, phase: 'postflight' }. Later WT rows declare all four plan paths too, so they are CONTESTED. They land without a wrapper-observed editing tool only if each path was clean at THIS session's pre-flight and every peerDeclared[].peerActive is false (mem:decision-contested-idle-peer-exception). If either fails, stop and comment on the task. Never hand-land or weaken attribution. Add: 1. cli mode: when WT_CLI_RECORD is set, also append one JSON line to that file: {cwd: process.cwd(), argv: process.argv.slice(3), env: MOE_PROJECT_PATH, MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET (null when unset), mcpConfig: the text of the file named after --mcp-config, else null}. An argv containing --version prints `0.0.0-fake` and records nothing. 2. Per-type shims named claude, codex, gemini and grok, each in its own directory under the suite root. The wrappers take the CLI type from the --command basename with the extension stripped. sh: `exec "" "" cli "$@"`. ps1: `.cmd` running `"" "" cli %*`, then `exit /b %errorlevel%`. Model both on the existing shim. 3. launch() takes an optional trailing options object {type, args}: type picks the shim, args are appended to the wrapper argv. Without it, launch() behaves as before. 4. The fixture's control gets an untracked .moe/agents/x.md. enableAgentTeams keeps its default, true. Cases. Each uses a fresh fixture with FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE for task-postflight, MOE_DISABLE_ARGV_PROBE=1, WT_CLI_RECORD=/record.jsonl and GROK_HOME=/grok-home. W is the workspace path, and same(a,b) compares fs.realpathSync.native of both sides, lower-cased on win32. launch-claude, launch-codex (--codex-exec / -CodexExec), launch-gemini (--gemini-exec / -GeminiExec) and launch-grok (--grok-exec / -GrokExec), as one loop. Assert: (a) Exit 0 and exactly one record. claude, gemini and grok record a cwd that is same() as W. codex's argv has -C followed by W (its working root), and grok's has --cwd followed by W. (b) MOE_PROJECT_PATH is same() as the control; MOE_WORKTREE_PATH is same() as W; MOE_TASK_BRANCH === 'moe/task/task-postflight'; MOE_LAND_TARGET === 'main'. (c) W holds the CLI's configs, each naming the control as the moe server's MOE_PROJECT_PATH: - sh: W/.mcp.json for every type (JSON mcpServers.moe.env.MOE_PROJECT_PATH); - W/.codex/config.toml or W/.grok/config.toml (the `MOE_PROJECT_PATH = "…"` line, its value JSON-decoded); - W/.gemini/settings.json (JSON); - ps1 claude: the record's mcpConfig, its temp --mcp-config. codex also gets W/.codex/agent-instructions.md, and gemini W/.gemini/GEMINI.md. (d) "Not rewritten", by banner count. For each writer banner the type prints, count log lines ` `. With backslashes read as slashes, a path ending in /.worktrees/task-postflight/ is W; any other path ending in / is the control. Expect exactly 1 each, or 2 each for the sh Gemini banner, which that writer prints twice per write. The banners are sh `Wrote project MCP config:` (every type) and, on both, `Codex MCP config written to:`, `Gemini MCP config written to:` and `Grok MCP config written to:`. Match the whole banner: ps1's claude line `MCP config written to:` is a suffix of the others. (e) W/.claude/agents holds exactly the .md names in /.moe/agents, each byte-equal (Buffer.equals). grok: /trusted_folders.toml has a [folders.'

'] header with same(p, W). config-fail (codex): before the launch, make W the way WT-04T's half-made case does (`worktree add --lock --reason "moe task-postflight" --no-checkout --no-track -b moe/task/task-postflight W main`). Then mkdir W/.codex/config.toml as a DIRECTORY. Assert refused('config-fail', 'MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED') and that no record file exists. Keep the suite's compact style, and assert every git call. implementationPlan.description:
sh wrapper, part 1, in scripts/moe-agent.sh: the writers become functions, plus the per-task worktree phase.

Save rule for EVERY moe-agent.sh save in steps 2-3:
- Never patch the live file in place. Running bash seats read it at stale offsets (mem:gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse, task-f31d415d).
- Build the whole new file as a copy on the SAME filesystem, e.g. /mnt/d/moe-scratch/c4cccb84/moe-agent.sh, and run `bash -n` on it.
- Check that the live file's sha256 is unchanged since you copied it, then make ONE `mv -f` onto scripts/moe-agent.sh.

1. Wrap the writers in place. Do not re-indent their bodies.
   - ensure_mcp_config's tail, from `    # Also write project-level .mcp.json`, becomes `write_project_mcp_json ROOT SERENA_PROJECT`, which writes ROOT/.mcp.json. ensure_mcp_config ends by calling it with "$PROJECT" "$SERENA_PROJECT".
   - The codex (~916), gemini (~1089) and grok (~1284) blocks become write_codex_config, write_gemini_config and write_grok_config. In each:
     - the `if [ "$CLI_TYPE" = … ]; then` line becomes the function header plus `local root="$1" SERENA_PROJECT="$2"`. The local shadows the global, so the body's Serena references need no edit;
     - the block's closing `fi` becomes `}`;
     - right after the function, the old site becomes `if [ "$CLI_TYPE" = codex ]; then write_codex_config "$PROJECT" "$SERENA_PROJECT" || exit 1; fi`, and the same for gemini and grok.
   - In the bodies only the file location moves. `$PROJECT/.<cli>` and `$PROJECT/.mcp.json` become `$root/…`, and grok's `grant_grok_folder_trust "$PROJECT"` takes "$root". The value written as the moe server's MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays "$PROJECT", the control, whatever ROOT is. `exit 1` becomes `return 1`.
   - Error handling: bash ignores set -e inside a function run from an `||` list. So add `|| return 1` to each body's mkdir and to its python heredoc command (`… << 'PYEOF' || return 1`). Otherwise a failed write over an existing file passes the `[ -f ]` check. Keep that check as well.
   - Keep the comment line `# For grok: write project-scoped .grok/config.toml (same [mcp_servers.*] TOML` verbatim. prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs ends its codex_moe_server_override slice there.
2. Per-iteration reset, beside `    MOE_TOP=""` (~6633), where WT-04 resets MOE_WT_*: `CLI_ROOT=""; unset MOE_WORKTREE_PATH MOE_TASK_BRANCH MOE_LAND_TARGET`. An empty CLI_ROOT means shared mode.
3. Define `prepare_worktree_launch` next to WT-04's provision_worktree. It does three things:
   - Sets CLI_ROOT="$MOE_WT_PATH" and exports MOE_WORKTREE_PATH="$MOE_WT_PATH", MOE_TASK_BRANCH="$MOE_WT_BRANCH" and MOE_LAND_TARGET="$MOE_WT_TARGET" (the claim's bare target).
   - Writes into CLI_ROOT what the pre-flight writes into the control for this CLI: write_project_mcp_json, then the CLI's own writer when CLI_TYPE is codex, gemini or grok. The grok writer grants grok folder trust for W.
   - Under the pre-flight agents mirror's gate (`"$ENABLE_AGENT_TEAMS" = true` and `$MOE_DIR/agents` present), runs `mkdir -p "$CLI_ROOT/.claude/agents"` and copies every `$MOE_DIR/agents/*.md` there with `cp -f`. Loop with a `[ -f ]` guard; an agents dir with no .md files is not a failure.
   Follow every writer, mkdir and cp with `|| worktree_stop MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED "<what> (<path>)"`. That is WT-04's refusal: it prints `[ERROR] CODE: detail`, calls report_blocked once, launches no CLI and exits 1. Call it directly, never inside $(...), a pipeline or a subshell. Nothing falls back to the control.
   The writers already read an exported MOE_DAEMON_HOST. Confirm it is exported by this point, so W's TOML needs no extra upsert.
   WT-06 will insert its Serena root and link step at the top of this function, before the writes. Leave no placeholder line.
4. Call it with `if [ "${MOE_WT_MODE:-}" = worktree ]; then prepare_worktree_launch; fi` directly after the `fi` that closes the `preflight_landing … launch` block (~7666), above `    # Compose final PROMPT`. That spot is outside the taskless-handoff slice, which ends at `    # -------- Pre-flight landing: recovery`.

Unchanged: the MOE_PROJECT_PATH export (~699), every RPC, the proxy path, the heartbeat sidecar, the prompt-cache check's "$PROJECT", and the stream parser's MOE_GIT_TOP, MOE_GIT_REL and MOE_SERENA_PROJECT_ROOT. Attribution inside W is WT-07.

ps1 wrapper, the twin of steps 2-3, in scripts/moe-agent.ps1, plus the ps1 side of scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs. Keep the wrapper UTF-8 with a BOM (parity-check enforces this). After saving, the ParseFile errors must be empty.

1. Writers. The chain `if ($cliType -eq "codex") { … } elseif (… "gemini") { … } elseif (… "grok") { … } else { Write-Host "MCP config written to: $mcpConfigFile" }` (~972-1377) changes in place, without re-indenting:
   - Each arm becomes Write-MoeCodexConfig, Write-MoeGeminiConfig or Write-MoeGrokConfig with `param([string]$Root, [string]$SerenaProject)`. PowerShell names are case-insensitive, so $SerenaProject shadows the script's $serenaProject and the bodies need no Serena edit.

   - In each catch, keep `Write-Error "Failed to write … MCP config: $_"` and replace `exit 1` with `throw`, so a call never exits the script by itself.
   - Below the three functions, a dispatch keeps today's order and arms. codex, gemini and grok call their writer with -Root "$projectPath" -SerenaProject $serenaProject; else keeps the Write-Host. An unhandled throw still ends the pre-flight with exit 1, as today's Write-Error under $ErrorActionPreference Stop does.
   - Function scope is safe: no block-local variable is read after the chain (checked 2026-10-30; $lines and $skip are reassigned before their later uses).
